title: Concordia Lutheran Health and Human Care was owned by Concordia Care Network in Q1 2026
text:
During the first quarter of 2026, Concordia Lutheran Health and Human Care was under the ownership of Concordia Care Network, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) reports . This Butler County nursing home has been operated by Concordia Care Network since September 1, 2022.
The facility is a non-profit organization.
In that quarter, the nursing home received a CMS overall rating of 2, which is lower than Pennsylvania’s state average nursing home rating of 3.0. CMS reviews facilities on aspects such as results from health inspections, available staffing, and resident care quality.
Records indicate Concordia Lutheran Health and Human Care provided services to an average of 134.7 residents daily in the first quarter of 2026, with a total bed capacity of 142. The home remains unaffiliated with any hospital.
Citing first quarter 2026 data, Concordia Lutheran Health and Human Care incurred 1 fine totaling $8,021 and received 1 penalty.
Butler County, Pennsylvania, is home to 5 non-profit nursing facilities overall.
U.S. Census Bureau estimates show that the nation’s population of older adults has consistently climbed while numbers among younger groups have dropped. Between 2020 and 2024, the count of Americans age 65 or older rose 13%, whereas those under 18 declined by 1.7%. Across a century, the older adult population increased dramatically , growing from 4.9 million in 1920 to more than 61 million by 2024.
A 2021 study finds that about half of adults in this group, or nearly 28 million people, could need long-term care services and assistance. The same research projects that over one-third are likely to require nursing home care later in life.
“Living a long life is something that many of us want and could get,” said Jesse Slome , executive director of the American Association for Long-Term Care Insurance, which educates on insurance. “But when we live a long life, the chances of us needing long-term care increase exponentially. But when you need that type of care, there are limited options.”
